transcript: Hamilton's Oak Onaodowan is starring alongside Aigner Mizzelle in this new play about MMA Fighting and siblings, and it kind of broke my heart. The Monsters is a new play written and directed by Ngozi Anyanwu about a pair of siblings who reunite after many years, at which point the brother begins to train his younger sister in MMA Fighting, we see their renewed but still complicated relationship evolve over the course of several years, interspersed with flashbacks from their troubled childhood. I thought the production here overall was really strong, from the raw, grounded performances of the two actors to the staging, which manages to feel dynamic and explosive while also being incredibly intimate. And I think the play really beautifully captures the tenuous balance of love and distance between these two siblings and how the circumstances of their history, both shared and unshared, inform how they engage with each other now. it does have its flaws, though. I think it starts to drag a bit in the latter half as it starts to —not exactly tread water— but maybe hits that pitfall where it's trying to make every scene feel like this big emotional gut punch, and it's a bit of a game of diminishing returns. Even still, though, a lot of those emotional gut punches really hit home. I did feel deeply moved by this play at various points and just invested in this relationship throughout. although I might be a bit biased because this type of sibling narrative does tend to strike a chord with me. There were facets of this play that I definitely found kind of relatable, even down to, like, the character names were a bit of a jumpscare for me. But in either case, I think this is overall a really strong and emotionally resonant piece. And it's playing at MTC Off broadway through March 22nd
